lectures.title: Delhi Sultanate: political history and administration

parts.t: Muhammad Ghori's invasions and the Ghurid conquests
items: Ghori defeated by Mularaja-II / Bhimdev-II; **Naika Devi** acted as regent; Mount Abu; Ghori's first defeat in India
**1st Battle of Tarain**: Prithviraj Chauhan vs Muhammad Ghori
Leader Prithviraj Chauhan; Chauhan victory, Ghori defeated
**2nd Battle of Tarain** (Tarain II): Muhammad Ghori vs Prithviraj Chauhan
Leader Muhammad Ghori; Ghori victory, Ghori defeated Prithviraj; reversal of Tarain I (1191)
**Battle of Chandawar**: Muhammad Ghori vs Jayachandra / Jaichand
Jayachandra defeated; Chandawar is near the Yamuna
**Bihar (1193–1203):** Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Bihar; Nalanda and Vikramshila destroyed; Odantpur captured.
**Bengal (1198–1203):** Bengal campaign of Bakhtiyar Khalji; Nadiya captured/entered; Lakshman Sen fled to East Bengal; Lakhnauti.
Coins of Mahmud Ghazni and Muhammad Ghori
**Mahmud Ghazni:** silver coins with Arabic on one side and Sanskrit on the other side; the Sanskrit is in the Sharada script.
**Muhammad Ghori:** coins with Goddess **Lakshmi** on one side and the Kalma in Arabic on the other side: a Muslim ruler's coins bearing Lakshmi.

parts.t: The five dynasties and their founders
items: **Delhi Sultanate:** capital Delhi, the main political centre (Delhi is associated with the Delhi Sultanate and was the Mughal political centre too).
**5 major dynasties:** Slave → Khalji → Tughluq → Sayyid → Lodi.
**Qutbuddin Aibak**, also regarded as the first ruler of the Slave dynasty
Succeeded the Slave/Mamluk dynasty: Khalji takeover
**Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**, also known as Ghazi Malik / Ghazi Tughluq
Succeeded the Khalji dynasty: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq
**Khizr Khan**, after taking control of Delhi in 1414 AD
Succeeded the Tughlaq dynasty: Khizr Khan
Succeeded the Sayyid dynasty: Bahlol Lodi

parts.t: Slave / Mamluk dynasty: Aibak, Iltutmish, Razia, Balban
items: **Contribution:** founded the Slave dynasty; Quwwat-ul-Islam; began the Qutub Minar.
Did not assume the title of Sultan
**Accession (1211, Delhi):** declared himself Sultan; the Turkish nobles supported/approved his succession after Qutbuddin Aibak.
**Contribution:** consolidated the Sultanate; Tanka + Jital; completed the Qutub Minar.
**Iqta system:** introduced by Iltutmish; revenue + military administration.
**Caliph's name on coins:** after the Caliph's recognition, Iltutmish put the Caliph's name on his coins.
**Genghis Khan (1221 CE):** the Mongol invasion / incursion under Genghis Khan reached the Indus during Iltutmish's reign: Genghis Khan's threat/entry into Indian history.
**Razia:** first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
**Blood and Iron Policy:** associated with Balban; strong monarchy and suppression of rebellion.
**Garhmukteshwar inscription:** in the Garhmukteshwar Mosque, Balban called himself “Helper of a Caliph”.

parts.t: Khalji dynasty: Alauddin Khalji and Mubarak Shah
items: **Alauddin Khalji (1296–1316):** market reforms; military reforms; southern expeditions.
**Associated with:** market/price control; Mongol defence; Chittor.
**Title:** Sikandar-i-Sani (Second Alexander, Sikandar II), inscribed on his coins.
**Mongols:** repeated Mongol invasions of the Delhi Sultanate in Alauddin Khalji's reign contributed to a large standing army and military/revenue reforms.
**Diwan-i-Mustakharaj:** Alauddin Khalji's revenue administration / recovery department, for land revenue.
**Abolished:** Alauddin Khalji abolished the privileges of the Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary.
**Mir Bakshi office:** introduced in the Khalji period; a military/administrative office.
**Mubarak Shah (Mubarak Khalji):** known as Al-Imam, Ul-Imam, Khilafatullah.
**Ghazi Malik:** Ghiyasuddin Tughluq, also known as Ghazi Malik / Ghazi Tughluq, founded the Tughluq dynasty.
**Mongol campaigns (1320):** Ghazi Malik defeated/chased the Mongols 29 times; later he became Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
**Contribution:** token currency; capital transfer to Daulatabad; Doab taxation.
**Capital shift:** Delhi → Daulatabad → Delhi; Daulatabad / Devagiri is the place linked with his capital transfer.
**Coin legend:** “Al Sultan Zilli Allah”, meaning the Sultan as Shadow of God.
**Ibn Battuta:** visited India in the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq; associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq and the Rihla.
**Haqq-e-Sharb:** Firuz Tughlaq's irrigation tax = 10% of the crop yield.
**Timur / Taimur (1398 CE):** invaded India and Delhi in 1398; the Delhi Sultanate was severely weakened; the ruler was Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq.
**Khizr Khan (1414):** defeated Daulat Khan in the Delhi succession, took Delhi and founded the Sayyid Dynasty.
**Bahlul Lodi:** founded the Lodi dynasty, which succeeded the Sayyid dynasty.
**Abolished:** Sikandar Lodi abolished the tax on grains / several grain levies.
Revenue assignment in the Delhi Sultanate
Branding of horses in Sultanate military administration
Founded Slave dynasty; Quwwat-ul-Islam; began Qutub Minar
Consolidated Sultanate; Tanka + Jital; completed Qutub Minar
First and only woman ruler of Delhi Sultanate
Market reforms; military reforms; southern expeditions
Token currency; capital transfer to Daulatabad

lectures.title: Delhi Sultanate: economy, society, literature, art and architecture

items: **Regular Sultanate coinage:** Iltutmish introduced regular coinage in silver + copper, with Delhi as capital.
**Tanka:** silver coin introduced by Iltutmish; the silver coin is mentioned as 175 grains.
**Khalifa's name on coins:** Iltutmish, after recognition by the Abbasid Caliph.
**Lakshmi + Arabic Kalma:** coins of Muhammad Ghori, a Muslim ruler's coins bearing Lakshmi.

parts.t: Alauddin Khalji: revenue measures and market policy
items: Revenue collection based on measuring land
First Sultan associated with systematic land measurement
Traditional tax-collection privileges abolished; revenue collected more directly
**Market / Price Control Policy (Alauddin's Market Policy):** control prices to support the maintenance of a large army at lower cost.

parts.t: Firoz Shah Tughlaq: canals and translations
items: **Firoz Shah Tughlaq:** associated with canals; irrigation; public works; Haqq-i-Sharb.
One of his major irrigation canals
**Translation Department:** Firuz Tughlaq had Sanskrit texts translated into Persian by various scholars; it promoted the exchange of ideas between communities.
**Nagarkot:** ~1300 Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi library were translated into Persian by Azizuddin Khan under Firuz Tughlaq.
**Ibn Battuta:** traveller of the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq; Sultanate-period observations; author of the Rihla.
**Crops of medieval India:** according to Ibn Battuta, rice could be cultivated thrice a year in suitable regions; wheat, sugarcane and cotton too could be cultivated thrice a year.
History of early Muslim rule; Bengal / Bakhtiyar Khalji
**Identity:** poet + historian + musician; called Tuti-i-Hind; born at Patiyali.
**Court:** Alauddin Khalji + several other Delhi Sultans (Delhi Sultanate courts).
**Kitab-ul-Hind / Tahqiq-i-Hind (Tarikh-i-Hind):** by Al-Biruni; it deals with Indian society, religion, culture, geography, science, customs and politics.
**Kitab Patanjal:** Al-Biruni translated Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra into Arabic under this title.
First major mosque of the Delhi Sultanate
One of the first Indo-Islamic buildings
Oldest monument in the Nizamuddin dargah complex
First tomb in purely Indo-Islamic style in India; first true arch

lectures.title: Vijayanagara Empire: political history and administration

items: **Founders:** Harihara I (Harihara-I) and Bukka I (Bukka Raya I) established the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 AD (1336 CE).
**The city:** Harihara I founded a new city on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra: Vijayanagara (modern-day Hampi).
**Capital:** Vijayanagara / Hampi, on the Tungabhadra River.

parts.t: The four dynasties and the succession
items: **Four dynasties in succession:** Sangama → Saluva → Tuluva → Aravidu.
Succeeded the Sangama dynasty: Narasimha Saluva, 1485
Succeeded the Saluva dynasty: Vira Narasimha
Succeeded the Tuluva dynasty: later Vijayanagara succession

parts.t: Sangama rulers: expansion and the army
items: **Kumara Kampana (c. 1370–71):** conquered Madurai in the Vijayanagara expansion; Madurai annexed to Vijayanagara; Madhura Vijayam → Ganga Devi.
**Harihara-II (1380):** captured Goa + Belgaum from the Bahamani in the Vijayanagara–Bahamani conflict; also expanded into Kanara, Mysore, Kanchi, Trichinapalli.
**Devaraya-I:** first Vijayanagara monarch to enlist Muslims in the army.
**Reign:** enthroned in 1509; reigned 1509–1529 CE; Vijayanagara's political/cultural zenith.
**Battle of Raichur (1520):** the greatest battle fought by Sri Krishnadevaraya.
**Udayagiri Fort:** after its conquest, Sri Krishnadevaraya took the idol of Balakrishnudu.
**Bhatkal (Karnataka):** port of Portuguese trade in the Vijayanagara period; Krishnadeva Raya permitted Afonso de Albuquerque / the Portuguese to construct a fort at Bhatkal (Bhatkal Fort).
**Portuguese:** the reign of Krishnadeva Raya saw Portuguese travellers / contacts with Vijayanagara.
**Nagalapuram:** founded by Krishnadeva Raya in honour/memory of his mother Nagala Devi.
**Battle of Tallikota / Talikota / Rakshasi-Tangadi (1565):** Vijayanagara vs the Deccan Sultanates; between the Adil Shahis of Bijapur and Ramaraya.
**Opposing forces:** combined Bijapur + Ahmadnagar + Golconda forces were among the major forces.
**Result:** Vijayanagara defeated; a watershed battle that weakened Vijayanagara.
**After Tallikota:** the capital of Vijayanagara shifted to Penugonda (Penukonda).
Italian traveller who visited South India / Vijayanagara; earliest European visitor to Vijayanagara
Portuguese traveller who visited the Vijayanagara Empire
**A Forgotten Empire:** book by Robert Sewell.

lectures.title: Vijayanagara Empire: economy, religion, literature, art and architecture

items: **Tanks / reservoirs:** associated with the Vijayanagara rulers; irrigation and water management.
**Porumamilla inscription:** of Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura; mentions 12 rules for tank construction.
**Virupaksha / Virupakshudu:** family god of the Vijayanagara people; famous temple at Hampi.
**Sayana:** famous commentator on Vedic texts (Vedic commentaries); Vijayanagara patronage.
**Krishnadeva Raya as patron:** patronised Telugu literature + scholars.
**Allasani Peddana:** court poet of Sri Krishnadevaraya.
Famous temple; South Indian temple tradition
Hazara Rama is the popular name of the Ramachandra temple
**Lepakshi Temple:** famous for the beautiful paintings of the Vijayanagara School (Lepakshi Paintings); Art of Vijayanagara = Lepakshi; Vijayanagara architecture.
**Stone bull:** a huge stone bull is located at Lepakshi.
**Penugonda Verupanna Virabhadeshwar Swamy temple:** constructed at Lepakshi.
**Tadipatri / Thadipatri (Chintala Venkata Ramana temple):** its gopuras excel in beauty over those of Hampi Vitthalaya, according to art critics.

corrections.corrected: Mahmud Ghazni: silver coins with Arabic on one side and Sanskrit on the other side; the Sanskrit is in the Sharada script.
corrections.checked: Mahmud's bilingual dirhams of Mahmudpur (Lahore) carry the Sanskrit legend in Sharada script (Wikipedia, Ghaznavid bilingual coinage: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghaznavid_bilingual_coinage)

corrections.title: Delhi Sultanate: economy, society, literature, art and architecture
corrections.rocket: Silver currency | Iltutmish | Silver | Silver coin mentioned as 175 gm
corrections.corrected: Tanka: silver coin introduced by Iltutmish; the silver coin is mentioned as 175 grains.
corrections.checked: The tanka's standard weight was 175 grains (about 11 g); surviving coins weigh c. 10.6-10.9 g (GKToday https://www.gktoday.in/question/the-175-gms-coin-issued-by-iltutmish-was-in-which ; Fitzwilliam Museum https://data.fitzmuseum.cam.ac.uk/id/object/93141)

corrections.rocket: Hazara Ramaswamy | Hampi | Constructed by Krishnadevaraya; Hazara Rama Temple | Krishnadeva Raya
corrections.corrected: Hazara Rama Temple (Hazara Ramaswamy), Hampi: builder Devaraya I.
corrections.checked: Inscriptions inside the temple show Devaraya I built it in the early 15th century (Vijayanagara Research Project, Penn Museum: https://www.penn.museum/sites/VRP/html/Ramachandra.html ; MAP Academy https://mapacademy.io/?p=3058). Note: many quiz sites repeat the Krishnadevaraya attribution.

corrections.corrected: Mir Bakshi office: introduced in the Khalji period; a military/administrative office.
